perfComments.author: xvotex
perfComments.body: Most likely, there simply isn’t enough physical space in the stash for separated sorting. I haven’t had any issues with separated mode on 4.0. I added this mode mostly for myself, since I play with the largest stash available. It’s far from optimal, but it makes the layout much easier to read visually. Adding a bunch more subcategories isn’t a problem, but it makes the sorting process more complicated. Separating every category in separated mode will spread items out as much as possible and take up a lot more stash space. Orientation adds another layer of conditions to the sorting process, which reduces sorting efficiency. This is exactly why the direction option (Asc/Desc) is disabled for size sorting, since sorting from smallest to largest is extremely inefficient. Adding orientation would most likely slow down the search for an optimal layout, and the resulting layout itself might also be less optimal. Sorting weapons is a massive pain in the ass… Because of their unusual sizes, I’ve rewritten the weapon sorting logic dozens of times, and it’s by far the slowest part of the sorting process.

perfComments.author: swiftduck
perfComments.body: Nice mod. I noticed some quirks. I dont mind them. This slows down some things but most things work in normal speed during the slowdown. Actors (including you) move in slow motion at the appropriate percentage of dilation specified in the BepInEx menu. SOME of your weapon animations slow down, most impactfully your manual cycling animations like bolt and lever actions. Turn speed is affected for you and bots. You move your gun slower. (they seem to as well but it matters less for them.) Rate of fire is not affected. You can set the dilation to .1 and mag dump a drum mag in less than a second (sort of) Item use is not affected. You can slow time and use up an entire grizzly before the scav gets around the corner. Projectile speeds are not affected. No neo shenanigans. Grenade timer is not affected. Throw a fused ‘nade with the dilation turned too far down and it will probably detonate in mid air right next to your face. ask me how i know this :D AI are only affected in that their movements are slowed. If they can move the gun to aim at you, they will mag dump you without regard to the time slow. They will ramp up their aim accuracy without regard to the slow time, too. It’s actually safer NOT to use the bullet time when caught out because you move slower but the bots don’t aim slower and the bullets dont move slower and the guns don’t fire slower. I did see a bot blow himself up with a grenade once. I did an entire raid in .1 dilation while having my morning coffee. weirdly chill experience. I died to a bot mag dump through a window from god knows how far away lol. This is very useful in short bursts for lining up long shots or head shots. You are in great danger if you stand in front of an aggressive bot and go slow-mo, though. It’s way less OP than i thought it would be and i now use it set at .4 just to give me a little edge in decisive shots. Great fun with this mod. Had a good time figuring out all the quirks of it.

perfComments.author: xxxxtok
perfComments.body: 5-Second Freezing Issue – Cause Identified I was experiencing a consistent freezing issue where my game would completely freeze for approximately 150 milliseconds (0.15 seconds) every 5 seconds. At first, I suspected that the periodic server requests to /ISB/spawn/progress and /Aishi/miniLabs/state were causing the freezes. I modified both DLLs to increase the request intervals from 5 seconds to 60 seconds, but unfortunately, this had no effect. The game continued to freeze every 5 seconds. After further investigation, I finally identified the actual cause. Cause of the Freezing Issue Item ID: a2c16b836b441dc953652bd6 Related Method: AishiKeys.AishiAnomalyS2.UnlockNearDoor() Suspected Problematic Code: UnityEngine.Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll() What appears to be happening: When this item is in the player’s inventory, the mod appears to scan Unity objects every 5 seconds to check for nearby doors. This operation seems to temporarily block the game’s main thread, causing a freeze of approximately 150 milliseconds every 5 seconds. I confirmed that removing this item from my inventory completely eliminated the periodic freezing. This strongly suggests that the object-scanning operation associated with this item is responsible for the issue. Possible Fix It might be possible to resolve this by optimizing the object search or caching the results instead of repeatedly calling Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll() every 5 seconds. Ideally, this would allow players to keep the item in their inventory and use its functionality without experiencing periodic freezes. I hope this information helps you identify and fix the issue!

perfComments.author: viper-9
perfComments.body: Thanks! QuestCodex doesn’t keep its own copy of your character — it reads the profile live from the SPT server’s memory on every request, so a stale level usually means the page is looking at a different server or profile than the game. A few things to check: On the Progress page, open the profile dropdown at the top and make sure your current character is selected. Reload the page (Ctrl+F5) rather than only using the refresh button. The button refreshes progress, but not the profile list. Make sure the browser address (e.g. https://127.0.0.1:6969/questcodex ) points to the same server your game connects to. If you have more than one SPT folder, or an old SPT.Server window is still running, close the others and restart the server. If you play through Fika, the page needs to come from the host’s server. If it still shows level 28 after that, please let me know your SPT version and whether you use Fika or another multiplayer mod.

perfComments.author: chazut
perfComments.body: Thanks for the detailed feedback! I’ve noted both suggestions, chaining nearby rush objectives and adding proper no-go zones. For Custom (Loot), the bot needs to reach the rush point before the looting phase starts. The loot radius controls where it searches once there, so increasing it won’t help validate arrival. Check that the point is on reachable ground at the correct height/floor. I can’t confirm what’s causing your timeout from the description alone. Negative forces push bots away from an area, but even -10 doesn’t guarantee they’ll stay out. There isn’t a strict no-go zone option currently. Some orbiting between main tasks is intentional. Bots follow the Zone Editor forces while looking for a reasonably short path to a main objective. Repeatedly calculating long-distance paths is expensive and can cause stutters, so this is a performance tradeoff. There’s also a fallback that forces them toward a main objective after a period without progress.

perfComments.author: ffloridamann
perfComments.body: OPTIMIZATION Thanks for Icebreaker, it’s a great map. I’ve been tracking down hitches in my SPT 4.1.6 install and found two small things in ManimalIcebreakerClient 1.1.3. They run on every map, not just Icebreaker. RenderEnvProbe is created on the first CameraManager.SetCamera and kept for the session, so it’s alive everywhere, the hideout included. The off-map PerfCensus causes a hitch during play. When you’re not on Icebreaker, RenderEnvProbe.Update calls TickVanillaPerfCensus(). About 60 s after you spawn on any other map (and in the hideout), it runs FindObjectsOfType<CullingGridContent>() and FindObjectsOfType<LODGroup>() and logs a [PerfCensus] warning. On Factory that found 24,518 LOD groups and caused a 53 ms frame in the middle of the raid. Could it run only when DiagHotkeys (or another debug option) is on? The off-map branch of RenderEnvProbe.Update runs every frame. Most of it is reset work that only needs to happen once, after leaving Icebreaker. It also calls IcebreakerAcoustics.IcebreakerLoaded() every frame, which reads every loaded scene’s name. That makes about 1.5 KB of garbage per frame on Factory. Doing the reset once when you leave the map, and checking for Icebreaker scenes on SceneManager.sceneLoaded / sceneUnloaded instead of every frame, would make the mod essentially free on other maps. For now I’m skipping the census locally with a one-method Harmony prefix, but a fix in the mod itself would help everyone. Happy to share timings if they’re useful. Thanks!

It is especially helpful in the SPTVR mod I am also working on. In flatscreen t∗∗∗∗∗ I usually get around 8GB VRAM usage, using this reduces it down to 6-7. In SPTVR I end up capping it out often at 9.7GB and it starts spilling over to RAM causing stutters and just overall bad performance. With this mod, it goes from 9.7GB to 7-8GB. I have no idea what it’s clearing out and I also have no idea why this is NEVER ran in B∗∗‘s code. (EDIT: took a closer look and it looks like B∗∗ does run it occasionally but it seems like only after a raid) From what I can tell when searching about the method I’m running in here, it is common practice in Unity games to run this when loading new scenes.
